statement: Every party that processes personal data for the organization is bound by a signed contract on file before processing starts. The contract limits the party to the organization's instructions and requires it to stop processing and erase the data when instructed. The processor register is reconciled with the contracts on file on a defined cycle. Proof is the processor register and the signed contracts.
why_asked: A processor with no contract, or with a contract that lets it use data for its own ends, makes the organization answerable for misuse it cannot stop.
how_to_ask: Ask for the processor register and a contract for each of a few processors. Look for the instruction limit and the stop-and-erase term. Example probe: "Show me your contract with the payroll provider and the clause that limits it to your instructions."
question: Does your organization bind every party that processes personal data for it, by signed contract, to act only on its instructions?
expected_evidence: Processor register; signed contracts for each processor; reconciliation records of register against contracts on file, for the audit period.
good_looks_like: Every processor on the register has a signed contract on file. Each contract limits processing to the organization's instructions and requires the processor to stop and erase data when told. Reconciliation finds no gaps.
test: Reconcile the processor register against contracts on file. Sample contracts and check for the instruction limit and the stop-and-erase term. Pass if every register entry has a signed contract and each sampled contract contains both terms.
baseline_risk: A processor handles personal data with no binding limits, so misuse or retention cannot be prevented or enforced.
applicability: Applies if the organization uses processors for personal data.
